chapter: Marriage, Chicago and arriving in New York
title: Not meeting Chicago's black musicians, and Leonard Feather's Hot vs. Cool
summary: She met few South Side musicians and first met Dizzy in the 1950s on Leonard Feather's Hot vs. Cool record with Jimmy's band.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Was that club located on the North Side?
It was on the South Side.
The South Side. That’s what I wondered, because how did that affect . . . did you meet people like . . . or maybe he was already . . . no, Milt Hinton and that group was already gone at that point.
I never met Milt until years later. I didn’t meet any of those people. I guess I met Dizzy in the ’50s.

In New York, because Leonard Feather had this great idea for a record date called Hot vs. Cool. Dizzy was on one side of it, and Jimmy and his band were on the other, and they all played the same tunes, like . . . Or maybe . . .

Maybe . . . I know “Muskrat Ramble” was one. I’ve got the record upstairs. It’s really a collector’s item. The idea was good, but I guess Leonard always had these . . . like Cats vs. Chicks. That was another one that he had. All these crazy things. I don’t know. I lost track there.
